title: First 100 low-machine candidates: German→Rarámuri facsimile headword/boundary review
provenance_note: AI-assisted visual collation against the Steffel 1809 facsimile for the first low-confidence cohort in deterministic source order. The low-machine tier contains a high proportion of running prose, internal examples, Rarámuri equivalents, and layout fragments. Direct collation places this cohort on printed pp. 301–314 despite OCR-derived estimates extending to p. 316. The facsimile is authoritative; Merrill et al. (2020, DOI 10.47807/UNISON.8) was consulted only as a secondary collation aid for difficult readings. Preserved OCR remains untouched. Review is not independent human/philological or linguistic validation.

notes.low_machine_behavior: This first low-confidence cohort confirms the expected shift in error profile: most false candidates are fragments of long descriptive articles or examples rather than plausible headwords.
notes.page_drift: The deterministic queue estimated printed pp. 301–316; direct facsimile collation places all 100 source fragments on pp. 301–314, with 52 machine-to-facsimile page corrections.
notes.catchword_disambiguation: `Drauſſen` appears as a catchword at the bottom of printed p. 312, but the reviewed article start represented by RHD-S1809-00343 begins at the top of printed p. 313.
